slides.teacher_cue: New sound — long /oʊ/. Two spellings: oa appears in the middle of a word (boat, road, coat), ow appears at the end of a word (snow, flow, grow). Same position rule as ai/ay: oa in the middle, ow at the end. Note: ow can also make /aʊ/ (as in cow) — that pattern comes later. For now: ow = /oʊ/.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /oʊ/ cleanly and understand the oa/ow position rule.
slides.correction_move: Model the position rule: oa in the middle — boat, road. ow at the end — snow, flow. Students sort. Preview: ow can also say /aʊ/ — but we will learn that later.
slides.observation_note: Watch for ow/oa spelling confusion and for pure /oʊ/ production — not diphthong drift.

slides.teacher_cue: Say grow — to get bigger. gr onset, ow at the end. Confirm /r/ in onset. Reveal and blend.

slides.teacher_cue: Say slow — not fast. sl onset, ow at the end. Reveal and blend.
